parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is fertilization?","marks":1,"answer":"In sexual reproduction the fusion of sperm and ovum is called fertilization."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Hibiscus called monoecious? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"In sexual reproduction two opposite gametes unite, one of them is male gamete and the other one is female gamete. The plants that develop both the gametes in the same body are called monoecious. Hibiscus has both male and female reproductive organs in the same flower. Hence, it is called monoecious."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the formation process of 'X' in figure 'P'.","marks":3,"answer":"The figure 'P' of the stem is female gametophyte and 'X' is embryo sac. The formation process of embryo sac is explained below: Near the micropyle of the nucellus tissue being nourished in the nucellus of an ovule, a cell starts to become larger. Its protoplasm is dense and the nucleus is comparatively large. The cell divides into four haploid cells through meiotic division. Every cell, except the lowest one, gets disintegrated. Growing gradually, the larger cell matures into an embryo sac. The nucleus of the cell is haploid. The nucleus divides and produces two nuclei. These two nuclei take positions in two opposite poles. Next, these two nuclei consecutively divide twice and result in four nuclei. In the next stage, two nuclei from the two poles come to the middle of the cell and get fused to cause the emergence of diploid secondary nucleus. The nuclei in the two poles turn into cells with some amount of cytoplasm. Collectively, the combined structure of the three cells near the micropyle is called the egg apparatus. In between the cells, the one occupying the middle place is the ovum, which is a little larger. This is called an egg cell and the other two are called synergid cells. The cells in the opposite pole to the egg apparatus are called antipodal cells. This is how the process of developing the embryo sac is done."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the role of figure 'P' in sustaining the existence of living organisms.","marks":4,"answer":"The figure 'P' of the stem is female gametophyte i.e. the ovary of the flower. This part plays an important role in maintaining the existence of the living world. Most of the flowering plants protect their heredity through sexual reproduction. The sexual reproduction of plants occur through the production of seeds. The seeds create new plants which protect their heredity. Inside the female gametophyte resides the ovary and the ovule. Through pollination, the mature pollen lands on stigma of a carpel. Then the pollen tube grows, penetrating the style and absorbs some liquid. Once the tips of the extended pollen tube enter the embryo sac, it ejects two male gametes into the embryo sac. One of them, meeting with egg, causes the emergence of a zygote. The other male gamete, mixing with the secondary nucleus, develops triploid endosperm cells. At maturity, the ovule with the endosperm and embryo turns into a seed. When the fruit is ripe, the seed also becomes ready to produce new plants. In a suitable stage, the seed germinates and produces new plant. Thus, figure 'P' plays role in sustaining the existence of living organisms.\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is aster-ray?","marks":1,"answer":"During the pro-metaphase stage of mitotic cell division, rays spread out from the two poles of centrioles. These type of rays are called aster rays."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What kind of flower is a bottle gourd flower?","marks":2,"answer":"A bottle gourd flower is considered a unisexual flower. Because unisexual flowers have either androecium or gynoecium but not both. In bottle gourd, the aforesaid characteristics of a unisexual flower are noticed. Thus, it is a unisexual flower."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How is gamete created in the figure-P? Describe.","marks":3,"answer":"The figure-P in the stem is anther. The way by which gamete is created in anther is described below — A male gamete is formed after pollen is germinated. After being matured, pollen grains start germination inside the pollen sac. The nucleus of pollen grain undergoes mitosis division and generates two dissimilar cells-one is much larger than the other. The larger cell is called tube cell and the smaller is called generative cell. The tube cell turns into pollen tube and division of generative cell gives rise to two male gametes."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"In case of the processes 'M' and 'N', the characteristics of one may be changed but the other remains unchanged–Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"The processes of 'M' and 'N' represent self-pollination and cross-pollination respectively. Only cross-pollination can cause the characteristics to alter, whereas self-pollination keeps the traits unchanged. This is analyzed below: Self-pollination can occur on the same flower or on two flowers of the same plant. The plant that develops in this way cannot make changes to their characters, and so the features of the species can be maintained. This means, self-pollination does not bring about any variation in species. This way, a species can maintain its purity. On the other hand, cross-pollination occurs between two distinct flowers of the same species. And, this type of pollination brings about variation in its species. As a result, the seed produced this way is born with new characteristics. The plant, which grows from that seed, also has new characteristics. Finally, it can be said that, in self-pollination the traits do not change whereas in cross-pollination the characteristics may change.\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is placenta?","marks":1,"answer":"The special organ through which the relationship between the growing fetus in the mother's uterus and the maternal-uterine tissue is established is called placenta."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What type of pollination occurs in papaya? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Cross-pollination occurs in papaya. When pollination occurs between flowers of two different plants of the same species, it is called cross-pollination. In the papaya plant, cross-pollination takes place between two different plants. As a result of such pollination, new characters are created in the papaya plant, the rate of seed germination increases, the seeds are more vigorous and new species are created."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Draw and label a part of a plant using P, Q, R and S.","marks":3,"answer":"P, Q, R S mentioned in the stem are calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium respectively. By using these, the marked diagram of a part of a plant i.e. a flower is drawn below— [There is a figure: Parts of a Flower]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Procreation of plants is possible as a result of mixing of cells developed by R and S.—Analyse it.","marks":4,"answer":"A 'R' and 'S' marked parts are androecium and gynoecium respectively. Plant reproduction is possible as a result of the union of stamens and stigma formed in androecium and gynoecium. It is analyzed below— The main material of plant reproduction is seed. Fertilization results in the union of the stamens and stigma to produce seeds. Androecium is formed within stamens, which are part of the corolla of a flower. Another consists of one or more stamens. Pollen is produced within the anther of the stamen, the nucleus of this anther divides to form the tube nucleus and the generative nucleus. The generative nucleus later divides to form two sperm cells. On the other hand, the gynoecium consists of ovary, style and stigma. Inside the ovary, one or more ovules are equipped with special rules. Female gonads or ova are formed in these ovules. Stamens and stigma produced in androecium and gynoecium participate directly in reproduction. That is, after pollination, the zygote unites with the zygote to form a zygote. The zygote or fertilized ovum later becomes the seed and embryo. Then new seedlings are formed by seed germination and plant propagation takes place. Thus, from the above discussion it is understood that plant reproduction takes place by the union of the cells formed in the androecium (R) and gynoecium (S).\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is thalamus?","marks":1,"answer":"Thalamus is a round whorl situated at the tip of floral axis where four other whorls are arranged one after another."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why monoecious plant is different from dioccious plant?","marks":2,"answer":"In sexual reproduction, two opposite gametes fuse together. One of these gametes is male gamete and the other one is female gamete. Plant in which both of these gametes are produced in the same individual is called monoecious plant. On the other hand, when types of reproductive cells are produced in separate bodies, those plants are called dioccious plants."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the development of 'X' in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"‘X’ mentioned in the stem is human zygote. The development of human zygote is explained below. The fertilized egg gradually passes along the oviduct to the uterus. Immediately after fertilization, cell division begins in the zygote. This is called cleavage. At the last stage of cleavage, the growing embryo arrives in the uterus. At this stage, this mass of cells of the growing embryo is called a blastocyst. The changes that happen in the uterus are very important for the development of the embryo. For the development of next stage of blastocyst the embryo has to be embedded in the inner wall of the uterus. So the blastocyst becomes embedded with the uterine wall. This process is called implantation. Embedded in the uterus, the embryo grows and turns into a human body. Time between implantation and childbirth is called pregnancy. At that time menstruation or menstrual cycle does not occur. The embryo or fetus develops in the uterus for 38-40 weeks."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the role of hormones in the process of the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The process mentioned in the stem is human reproduction. Reproductive hormones secreted from endocrine glands within the body are - (1) Pituitary gland (2) Thyroid gland (3) Adrenal gland (4) Testis (5) Ovary (6) Placenta. Their role is explained below — The growth stimulating hormone and the producer hormone are produced by the pituitary gland. These hormones regulate growth of reproductive glands' secretions and functions and control mammary gland and milk secretion. These hormones also regulate the contraction of uterus. The thyroid glands secrete thyroxin hormone. This regulates metabolic function, and ensures physical and mental development, and sexual characteristics. Hormones secreted from the adrenal gland regulate development of the reproductive organs, and exposition of sexual characteristics. Testosterone hormone secreted from the testis and androgen help to produce sperms and secondary sexual characteristics, such as: deepening of the voice and growth of a beard. The Ovary secretes estrogen, progesterone, and relaxing hormones. These hormones cause the development of sexual characteristics, such as: menstruation, enlargement of the well of uterus for implantation of the embryo and placenta. It also has a particular role in the formation of the ovum. Gonadotropic and progesterone of placenta stimulate duetless glands of the ovary and help in enlargement of mammary glands.\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is cleavage?","marks":1,"answer":"The division of cells after fertilization in the early developmental state of the embryo is called cleavage."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why external fertilization is different from internal fertilization?","marks":2,"answer":"Fertilization is a biological process. In sexual reproduction, the fusion of the ovum and sperm is called fertilization. Fertilization is of two types: (i) external fertilization; and (ii) internal fertilization. External fertilization takes place outside of the body but internal fertilization takes place inside reproductive organs of females. Usually, external fertilization is limited to animals that live in water such as: different types of fish, frogs etc. On contrary, internal fertilization is the characteristic feature of most of the terrestrial animals. Hence, external fertilization is different from internal fertilization."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the gamete formation process in 'O' marked part in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The O marked part of the stem is an ovule. The female gamete or the megaspore required for the sexual reproduction of plants is formed here and the process is known as megasporogenesis. Near the micropyle being nourished in the nucleus of an ovule, a cell starts to become larger. Its protoplasm is dense and the nucleus is comparatively larger. The cell divides into four haploid cells through meiotic division. Every cell except the smallest one gets disintegrated. Growing gradually, the larger cell matures into an embryo sac. The nucleus of the cell is haploid. The nuclei are evolved as the nucleus divides. These two nuclei take position in two opposing poles. Next, these two nuclei consecutively divide twice and result in four nuclei. In the next stage, two nuclei from the two poles coming at the middle of the cell get fused and cause the emergence of two haploid secondary nuclei. The nuclei in the two poles turn into cells with some amount of cytoplasm. Collectively, the combined structure of the three cells near the micropyle is called egg apparatus. In between the cells, the one occupying the middle place is the ovum, which is little larger. This is called an egg cell and the other two are called synergid cells. The cells in the opposite pole to the egg apparatus are called antipodal cells. This way the process of developing embryo sac is ultimately done."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Compare the result of 'M' and 'N' process in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The M and N processes are called self-pollination and cross-pollination respectively. The transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of the same flower or the stigma of another plant of the same species is called pollination. This is the precondition for the development of fruits and seeds. Pollination is of two types – (i) self-pollination; and (ii) cross-pollination. Air, water, insects, birds, bats, snails, even humans act as the medium of pollination. The two types of pollination are compared below: | Feature | Self-pollination | Cross-pollination | |---|---|---| | Definition | If pollen transfer occurs on the same flower or the two flowers of the same plant then the type of pollination is called self-pollination. | When the attachment of pollen occurs in between two distinct flowers of the same species, it is called cross-pollination. | | Wastage of pollen | Wastage of pollen is less | Large waste of pollen | | Carrier dependency | Does not depend on a career for pollination | Carrier dependent process | | Purity | Purity of the species is maintained | Purity of the species is impaired | | New variety | No emergence of new variety | Emerge of new variety |\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is antipodal cell?","marks":1,"answer":"The cells on the opposite side of the egg apparatus are collectively called the antipodal cells."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"In which pollination the wastage of pollen is minimized? Explain it.","marks":2,"answer":"Self-pollination reduces pollen wastage. Because this pollination process takes place in the same flower or between two different flowers of the same plant. In this case one does not have to depend on the carrier for pollination. As a result, pollen wastage is reduced."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the formation process of germ cell from Figure-B with diagram.","marks":3,"answer":"Figure-B shows the anther, where the pollen grains reside. Pollen carries a haploid (n) nucleus. After pollination, the pollen nucleus divides by mitosis. This division produces a large nucleus and a small nucleus. The larger one is known as the tubular nucleus and the smaller one as the generative nucleus. The tubular nucleus enlarges into the pollen and the generative nucleus divides by mitosis to form two haploid (n) male gametes."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Both X and Y processes have advantages and disadvantages—Analyze it.","marks":4,"answer":"The two processes X and Y shown in the diagram of the stem are self-pollination and cross-pollination, respectively. Self-pollination and cross-pollination have several advantages and disadvantages. The advantages and disadvantages of both the processes are analyzed below— Advantages: Self-pollination reduces pollination waste. Such pollination does not require reliance on carriers and pollination is assured. Self-pollination does not change the characteristics of the new plant, so it is possible to maintain the characteristic purity of a species through this pollination. Cross-pollination, on the other hand, results in the development of new characters, increased seed germination rates, increased seed vigor, and the creation of new species. The new plants created in this process are highly adaptable. Disadvantages: Self-pollination results in reduced seed viability. Such pollination reduces the adaptability of the new generation of plants and can quickly lead to the extinction of a species. On the other hand, since cross-pollination is a carrier-dependent process, pollination is not guaranteed, resulting in a lot of pollen wastage. Cross-pollination destroys the purity of the species.\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is placenta?","marks":1,"answer":"The placenta is an organ that develops in the uterus during pregnancy. This structure provides oxygen and nutrients to a growing baby. It also removes waste products from the baby's blood."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why AIDS is called fatal disease?","marks":2,"answer":"AIDS is a type of illness caused by HIV infection. AIDS is fatal disease because it weakens the immune system and the body will be prone to a lot of communicable diseases which last for a lifetime and leads to death."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Draw the labelled diagram of different stages of formation of gametophyte of figure 'R'.","marks":3,"answer":"Figure 'R' is known as ovary. Similar to the Creative Question-Answer No. 14(c)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the roles of 'P' and 'Q' of the above stem for protection of plant generation.","marks":4,"answer":"For the protection of plant generation fertilization is necessary which keeps continuity of the reproduction. 'P' and 'Q' of the above stem are known as androecium and gynoecium respectively. These play a great role in the fertilization. Fertilization is a process of sexual reproduction, which occurs after pollination and germination. In flowers, the mature pollen grain from the androecium germinates after the pollination of the carpel of gynoecium and grows into the style by creating the pathway for the pollen grain to move down to the ovary. The pollen tube opens into the ovule through the micropyle and bursts into the embryo sac. Here, the male nucleus unites with the nucleus of an egg inside the ovule forming a diploid zygote, which later swells up and develops into fruits and seeds. Thus, seeds are source of reproduction of plants which protect its generation by carrying the characteristics of parents to their offspring from generation to generation.\n---"}]

After eight weeks, the embryo is more developed and the organs remain in small figure. This stage of embryo is called fetus. After 28 weeks fetus gets completion. After 38 weeks the full fetus becomes ready to be delivered."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the importance of the mentioned organ in the growth and proper development of embryo.","marks":4,"answer":"The temporary organ that forms relationship between embryo and mother is placenta. The importance of placents is immense in the proper development of embryo. The importance is explained below: The special organ through which the fetus in the uterus is connected to the tissue of the mother is called placents. Implantation is completed within 4-5 days after the embryo reaches the uterus. Some cells of the developing embryo along with the endoderm of the uterus compose an oval shaped and blood vessel enriched placenta. The placenta acts more or less like a lung. The dissolved oxygen in the blood of the maternal blood diffuses into the fetal blood and exchanges carbon dioxide from the fetus to the mother. The placenta also acts as kidney; metabolic waste product is diffused from the embryonic blood capillaries into the mother’s blood stream. In this way the waste products are eliminated. The placenta produces some important hormones which protect the embryo and helps in normal development. Placenta contains a huge amount of blood capillaries. The embryo is attached to the placenta by a tube called the umbilical cord. It is a tube through which the exchange of different materials occur between mother and fetus. At the time of pregnancy, it secretes some hormones which helps to produce milk and facilitate child birth. At the time of child birth the placenta is eliminated from the body.\n---"}]

Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The androecium is the third and an essential whorl of a flower. Pollen grains are produced in the anther of this whorl. The pollen grains then produce male gametes, which combine with the female gametes through fertilization to form zygotes. The resulting zygote later forms the embryo. That is, the androecium is called the essential whorl because it directly participates in the reproduction."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"How ‘X’ of the stem developed? Explain with figure.","marks":3,"answer":"X part mentioned in the stem indicates the egg. This egg is produced in inside the ovary of flower. The formation process of the egg is illustrated below. Near the micropyle being nourished in the nucellus of an ovule, a cell starts to become larger. Its protoplasm is dense and the nucleus is comparatively large. The cell divides into four haploid cells through meiotic division. Every cell except the lowest one gets disintegrated. Growing gradually, the larger cell matures into an embryo sac. The nucleus of the cell is haploid. The nucleus divides and forms two nuclei. These two nuclei take position in two opposing poles. Next, these two nuclei consecutively divide twice and result in four nuclei. In the next stage, two nuclei form the two poles coming at the middle of the cell get fused and cause the emergence of two haploid secondary nuclei. The nuclei in the two poles turn into cells with some amount of cytoplasm. Collectively, the combined structure of the three cells near the micropyle is called egg apparatus. In between the cells, the one occupying the middle place the ovum, which is little larger. This is called an egg cell and the other two are called synargid cells. The cells in the opposite pole to the egg apparatus are called antipodal cells. This way an egg the process of developing an egg is ultimately done."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"How ‘Y’ of the figure keep role after fertilization for the survival of living organisms. The cotyledon, radicle and plumule are developed one after another and the secondary nuclei start to make the endosperm. These seeds keep their species alive for generations. Therefore, it can be said that the subsequent change after fertilization of Y part protects the fauna.\n---"}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called hormone?","marks":1,"answer":"Hormones are defined as the chemical substances secreted from endocrine glands that are carried by blood and control various physiological processes."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is the immune system of the victim of AIDS destroyed?","marks":2,"answer":"AIDS is caused by HIV. The virus damages white blood cells and interferes with the production of blood cell antibodies. As a result, the number of white blood cells and the amount of antibodies gradually decrease. Due to this, the body's ability to resist disease is lost. Hence the immune system of the victims of AIDS is destroyed."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the continuous changes mentioned in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The continuous change mentioned in the stem indicates the development of a foetus after the fertilization of a sperm and ovum. The changes are explained here- 36 hours after the fertilization, the zygote undergoes the first cell division and form a two-cells structure. 16 cell structure or morula is formed approximately 72 hours later. In a few days, the ball of cells settle in the uterus. After 4 weeks, the embryo floats in a fluid-filled sac. The heart starts beating and brain starts to develop. After 5 weeks, it develops buds that will grow into arms and legs. After 8 weeks, the organs are all small in size. It is then called a foetus. After 28 weeks, the foetus is fully developed and 38 weeks after fertilization, the foetus becomes prepared for birth."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the role of the special organ mentioned in the stem for proper development of embryo.","marks":4,"answer":"Placenta is the special organ mentioned in the stem that connects the uterine tissue and the fetus. The role of placenta in the development of embryo is immense. This is analyzed below. A particular organ built up of maternal and fetal tissue which forms a special connection jointly is called a placenta. The embryo is implanted into the uterine wall with the help of the placenta. The embryo needs food for its growth. Carbohydrate, (glucose), protein (amino acid), essential minerals, water etc. are transferred from maternal to fetal blood to nourish the developing embryo. The placenta acts more or less like a lung. The dissolved oxygen in the blood of the maternal blood diffuses into the fetal blood and exchanges carbon dioxide from the fetus to the mother. The placenta also acts as kidney; metabolic waste products are diffused from the embryonic blood capillaries into the mother’s blood stream. In this way the waste products are eliminated. The placenta produces some important hormones which protect the embryo and helps in normal development. Placenta contains a huge amount of blood capillaries. This is how placenta plays important in the development of embryo.\n---"}]

Fertilization is the union of male gametes and eggs in the sexual reproduction of plants. The result of the fertilization process is explained below-Fertilization is a biological process. It is essential for sexual reproduction in all living things. It usually occurs after pollination in flowering plants. As a result of this process, various changes take place between the fertilized egg and the ovum and ovary. After fertilization, the ovule becomes a seed as a result of rapid growth, development and change. Inside the fertilized egg turns into an embryo and the ovary becomes a fruit. Later, mature seeds germinate and give birth to new plants and protect the flora. That is, fertilization plays a direct role in the reproduction of plants. If the plants that reproduce through sexual reproduction, do not get fertilized, their reproduction will become impossible. This can lead to the disappearance of flowering plants from nature. Again, the animals are completely dependent on plants for food and beautiful environment. Different types of fruits and seeds are used as animal food. If the extinction of flora in nature occurs, fauna will also be endangered."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"As per the stem what impact will occur in living world in absence of 'M' process? But humans, including most of the world's animals depend on the fruits, seeds, etc. of plants. As a result, if these plants become extinct, all the animals that depend on different parts of the plant will also suffer from instability. In this situation, in nature, there will be severe damage to biodiversity. Nature will lose its balance. Thus, if this pollination does not happen at some point, the entire fauna of the earth may be destroyed. Therefore, from the above discussion, it can be deduced that without the process M i.e. pollination, the living world will have adverse effects."}]
